text:
incident-bot: URGENT: Multiple Route53 healthchecks failing in us-west-2 for api.redwood-inference.com. Alert count: 42 in 5m. Paging on-call. Possible regional DNS / healthcheck flap. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incident/runbooks/dns-failover

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident created PD-38192, priority: P1.

sasha_oncall: ack — I'm on it. starting triage now. @jared_infra can you check gateway/ALB logs for 5xx spikes?

jared_infra: looking at ALB logs now. I see increased 504/502 from targets in us-west-2 around 14:02-14:07 UTC. pattern: client->alb OK, target responses timeout. samples: `alb-request-id: 7f3a2cbd`

maya_sre: i'm seeing monitoring probes from our probe fleet drop to 0 in us-west-2 at 14:00 UTC. metrics stopped shipping to datadog for that AZ group. could be probe agent crash or network egress problem.

jim_network: quick checks on control plane: no control-plane maintenance in us-west-2 in the window per cloud-notices. route tables look fine. doing traceroutes to a few targets.

sasha_oncall: customer impact? ellie, any CS reports?

ellie_custsuccess: two customers reported intermittent 503s around 14:05 UTC, one on mobile app and one via SDK. both are in west coast NA. Ticket links: CS-9054, CS-9055. No broad hits reported yet but they see elevated errors in their logs.

jared_infra: quick root cause hypothesis: backend targets healthy but probe/healthcheck failures cause ALB to mark unhealthy then traffic bounces. However probes are missing telemetry, so we might be reacting to stale probe data.

maya_sre: confirmed: our monitoring egress IPs were rate-limited by route53 healthcheck infra? Not sure. Also note our probe agent logs show repeated "unable to send heartbeat: connection refused" starting 14:00. attaching snippet:

```
# /var/log/probe-agent.log
14:00:02 WARN transport: dial tcp 52.94.76.1:443: connect: connection refused
14:00:07 WARN transport: dial tcp 52.94.76.1:443: i/o timeout
14:01:15 ERROR heartbeat: send failed: no route to host
```

jim_network: those IPs belong to upstream monitoring collectors in us-west-2 — i see intermittent loss on one of the transit links between our VPC and the cloud provider region edge. I'm opening a ticket with provider.

aws-support-bot: Support case opened: 1234567890. Initial response ETA 30-45m. Case link: https://console.aws/support/cases/1234567890

sasha_oncall: mitigation plan options — 1) failover DNS to eu-west-1 (low-ttl) for affected api.* endpoints, 2) temporarily raise ALB healthcheck thresholds to avoid rapid target cycling, 3) route traffic to Dedicated zone (if capacity) via feature flag. Pros/cons?

jared_infra: i'm in favor of raising healthcheck thresholds + short TTL DNS shift as fallback. raising thresholds is quick and reversible. Command to patch ALB healthcheck (example):

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-api/abcd1234 --health-check-interval-seconds 15 --health-check-timeout-seconds 10 --healthy-threshold-count 4 --unhealthy-threshold-count 10
```

maya_sre: we'll also unmute related monitors so we can see raw signal, then temporarily increase aggregation window to reduce noise. I'm patching monitors now.

sasha_oncall: doing the ALB patch now. will post output.

[~14:12] sasha_oncall: patched target-group thresholds. ALB now showing fewer target deregistrations. still seeing a handful of 5xx, but trend down.

pagerduty: Auto-suppression: Multiple similar alerts suppressed in the last 2m. Manual escalation still required.

jared_infra: starting a controlled DNS failover test to eu-west-1 for a small subset using Route53 weighted policy (weight 10 -> eu-west-1). command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://failover-shift.json`

sasha_oncall: confirm DNS TTL set to 30s for the shift. informing ops teams.

ellie_custsuccess: notifying the two affected customers we are actively mitigating, providing ETA ~45m.

aws-support-bot: Update: we've triaged the transit link; there's packet loss between provider edge and our monitoring collectors affecting TLS sessions. Engineering team investigating routing flaps.

jim_network: provider suggests rerouting via alternate edge POP. executing BGP announcement change with partner to avoid the affected transit. minimal impact expected.

[~14:28] maya_sre: after threshold change & partial dns shift, monitoring shows healthy responses from eu-west-1 and decreasing error rates in us-west-2. probe telemetry still partial — some collectors still show gaps.

sasha_oncall: good. escalate to review post-incident: why probes failed to send telemetry and why ALB healthcheck behavior led to target churn instead of grace. create follow-ups: MON-142 (probe resiliency), INFRA-331 (healthcheck failover tuning).

jared_infra: note: we should add synthetic checks that bypass the probe fleet (direct) to avoid single point of telemetry failure.

ellie_custsuccess: customers acknowledged the mitigation and are monitoring. one customer downgraded severity after partial recovery.

sasha_oncall: handoff — maya_sre will take ownership for the next shift (14:40-18:00 UTC) to watch for recurrence, continue AWS support case, and coordinate postmortem. I'm moving to advisory-only.

maya_sre: ack. I'll keep the case open and collect probe logs + collector egress traces, and coordinate a PID with network to harden egress paths.

jared_infra: leaving a smoke-check snippet for oncall:

```
# quick smoke
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
# expect 200 and <0.35s
```

sasha_oncall: incident status: mitigated (partial). customer impact reduced via DNS failover & ALB thresholds. AWS case open: 1234567890. Followups: MON-142, INFRA-331. postmortem owner: sasha_oncall.

incident-bot: Incident PD-38192 status updated to "Mitigated" by sasha_oncall. Please file postmortem within 72h.

pagerduty: Incident closed for on-call after handoff.

maya_sre: adding note — we found evidence of probe-agent doS from misconfigured retry loop on collector that exacerbated the TCP resets; will include root cause analysis in postmortem.

ellie_custsuccess: I'll follow up with affected customers with a summary once the postmortem draft is ready.

sasha_oncall: thanks team. leaving the thread open for any late signals. if anything flares, @pagerduty will page. :white_check_mark:
